races.name: Southwell Cardinal Conditions Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Golden View
runners_data.note: Front runner with class edge, 127 days off but Appleby/Buick combination excels with returning horses, proven on all-weather surfaces
runners_data.comment: Pulled well clear with a subsequent winner on his debut at Kempton (7f); has strong claims
runners_data.spotlight: Dam 7f-1m winner (including 2yo/AW/German Group 3; RPR 107); made a winning debut when sent off odds-on favourite at Kempton (7f, AW) in December, pulling well clear with the runner-up who has won since; should have no problem with this step up in trip and he looks a strong challenger to Yazin.

runners_data.name: Intense Vision
runners_data.note: Unknown quantity after 184-day break, unbeaten in France but facing stronger opposition, jockey Peate has limited big-race experience
runners_data.comment: 2-2 in France, winning over 6.5f and 1m on soft ground; makes his stable/British debut
runners_data.spotlight: Dam 7f 2yo winner (RPR 90); 2-2 in France, winning a maiden at Craon (6.5f, soft) in September then a conditions event at Bordeaux Le Bouscat (1m, very soft) in October; has been off since and now makes his stable/British debut having been purchased for 60,000gns; watch the betting.

runners_data.name: Yazin
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who needs to bounce back from poor Newmarket effort, Moore booking suggests connections confident, similar going form mixed
runners_data.comment: Made it 2-3 when winning at Newmarket (form franked); the one to beat on his return
runners_data.spotlight: Built on his debut effort when ending up a comfortable winner at Redcar (7f, good to soft) in September; took another step forward when winning a novice under a penalty at Newmarket (7f, good) in October when last seen, form that has been franked with six of those behind winning since; had wind surgery since; stepping up in trip should prove no issue and he looks the one to beat on his return.

races.paceDynamic: Golden View will take the early lead from his prominent position with no other confirmed pace pressers in this small field. The Charlie Appleby runner can dictate comfortable fractions through the middle sections without serious pressure from Yazin or Intense Vision tracking behind. With only three runners and minimal early pace, this sets up as a tactical affair where the leader can control the tempo and kick when ready. This race shape strongly favours front runners and prominent racers who can position close to the pace from the start.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Golden View Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Golden View breaks cleanly and establishes an uncontested lead
scenarios.body: He can dictate ideal fractions and has the class edge to kick clear when Buick asks, with his debut win showing he handles pressure well. The lack of early pace pressure allows him to conserve energy for a decisive move.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tactical Battle Develops
scenarios.trigger: If Yazin or Intense Vision challenge Golden View early for the lead
scenarios.body: The pace quickens earlier than expected, potentially setting up a late charge from whichever horse settles best. Golden View's stamina could be tested if pressed throughout.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Slow Pace Sprint
scenarios.trigger: If all three settle and nobody wants the lead early
scenarios.body: It becomes a sprint from the furlong pole where raw speed and tactical positioning matter most. Golden View's proven acceleration gives him the edge in a dash.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Intense Vision Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the French import shows significantly improved form on return
scenarios.body: His two wins in France suggest untapped potential, and the long break could have him primed for a bold showing. The small field suits a horse needing a clear run.

watchPoints.text: Golden View's fitness after 127 days off - any signs of rustiness early could open the door for his rivals
Intense Vision's market move - any significant support suggests the French form translates better than ratings suggest
Yazin's early positioning - Moore will need to get him close to dispute with Golden View to have any realistic chance
The pace through the first half-mile - if it goes too slow it could neutralize Golden View's main advantage
Golden View's response when first challenged - his debut win showed he could quicken but this is a step up in class

races.name: Celebrate With Sponsorship At Southwell Racecourse Handicap

runners_data.name: Blue Deveron
runners_data.note: Natural front runner returning from 28-day break with proven course and distance form, will dictate the pace unchallenged early.
runners_data.comment: Beaten a neck over C&D on debut and this drop back to 5f should suit on h'cap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten a neck over this C&D in January on debut but he failed to build on that at Wolverhampton next time; left the impression this drop back to 5f would suit when third at Chelmsford (6f, AW; second has won since) 28 days ago; contender on this handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Believeinmenow
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with disappointing recent form but competitive nursery effort suggests ability remains intact.
runners_data.comment: Failed to progress from his debut last year but ran respectably at Bath on his return
runners_data.spotlight: Failed to progress from his promising debut last year but he was beaten only 3l when ninth of 19 in a competitive nursery at York (6f, good to firm; first-time hood) last August; had been gelded prior to a a respectable reappearance at Bath (5f, good; raced freely) 18 days ago; now makes his AW debut with solid claims.

runners_data.name: Life After Love
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with two wins from three runs at this distance including course and distance success 28 days ago.
runners_data.comment: Form figures of 121 over 5f (both wins over C&D); respected off this 4lb higher mark
runners_data.spotlight: Has form figures of 121 over 5f, with both of the wins coming over this C&D, the most recent by a neck 28 days ago; the third has won since and she's respected off this 4lb higher mark.

runners_data.name: Beach Partee
runners_data.note: Another hold-up type who won three times previously but disappointed last time at Bath on turf.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up at Lingfield in January but failed to beat a rival on his stable debut
runners_data.spotlight: Won three times for William Knight, two of which came on the AW; runner-up at Lingfield (5f) in January but he failed to built a rival at Bath (5f, good) on his stable debut 18 days ago; needs to take a step forward from that effort.

runners_data.name: Sands Of Seve
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who made all to win last time in first-time visor, suggesting improved gate speed.
runners_data.comment: Got off the mark in a first-time visor at Wolverhampton last month; disappointing latest
runners_data.spotlight: Got off the mark when making all in a first-time visor at Wolverhampton (5f, AW) last month but he was comfortably held at Lingfield 27 days ago having been raised 9lb for that success; needs to bounce back.

races.paceDynamic: Blue Deveron will take them along as the sole natural front runner, setting what should be a sustainable pace without early pressure. Believeinmenow and Sands Of Seve are likely to track in second and third, while Life After Love and Beach Partee will drop towards the rear from their hold-up styles. With minimal early pace pressure, the tempo will be honest but not frantic, setting up a sprint finish over the final furlong. This race shape strongly favours the hold-up horses who can produce late kicks, as they'll benefit from the solid pace and have fresher finishing speed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Blue Deveron sets moderate fractions without early pressure
scenarios.body: The sustained pace will perfectly suit Life After Love and Beach Partee who can unleash superior finishing kicks. Both hold-up specialists have winning form at this distance and will benefit from the race setup.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Blue Deveron gets soft fractions and kicks clear
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace pressure allows him to dictate terms and his 28-day break may have sharpened him up. He was only beaten a neck on debut over course and distance.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Believeinmenow or Sands Of Seve get perfect positioning
scenarios.body: Tracking the leader closely gives them first run at the pacesetter while avoiding traffic problems. Sands Of Seve's front-running win last time shows he has gate speed to position well.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Blue Deveron goes too slow and the field bunches
scenarios.body: A crawling pace negates the hold-up horses' advantages and turns it into a lottery sprint from the furlong pole. The most naturally speedy horse with tactical pace wins.

watchPoints.text: Life After Love needs a strong pace to be effective - if Blue Deveron goes too slowly her hold-up style is compromised
Blue Deveron's 28-day break could either sharpen him up or leave him needing the run in a competitive field
Sands Of Seve's visor is retained after his front-running win suggesting connections want him more alert early
Beach Partee disappointed on turf last time and needs to prove AW form translates back to this surface
Believeinmenow drops back to 5f after struggling at 6f which may unlock improvement

races.name: Dog Friendly Raceday Tues 2nd June Handicap

runners_data.name: John Galt
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with solid recent consistency at this level but needs strong pace to be effective from the back

runners_data.name: Swinging London
runners_data.note: Dual course and distance winner whose hold-up style relies on others providing the gallop his finishing kick requires
runners_data.comment: Dual C&D winner who was unfortunate not to go closer at Pontefract last time; good claims
runners_data.spotlight: Dual C&D winner; beaten 2l when fourth of six here last month and he was unfortunate not to go even closer when fourth of 12 at Pontefract (1m4f, good to soft; short of room late on) 16 days ago; switches back to the AW with a good chance.

runners_data.name: The Truant
runners_data.note: Only prominent runner who can control the race completely but must prove his stamina reserves hold up at age nine
runners_data.comment: Five-time winner in Ireland; gives impression he may come on from his return at Kempton
runners_data.spotlight: Five-time winner in Ireland (hurdles/Flat) but he was well held in two starts for this yard at the end of last year; however, he seemed to be going quite well at the top of the straight before weakening into seventh at Kempton (2m, AW) 17 days ago and may take a step forward from that return to action.

runners_data.name: Vaguely Royal
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer without a Flat win since 2022 who faces a tactical disadvantage in this pace-light scenario
runners_data.comment: Well held at Lingfield last time and is without a win on the Flat since the end of 2023
runners_data.spotlight: Didn't run too badly when sixth here over 2m2f on his penultimate start but he was well held at Lingfield (2m, AW) 20 days ago; without a win on the Flat since the end of 2023 and needs to bounce back.

runners_data.name: Captain Brett
runners_data.note: Long-absent hold-up runner returning after 257 days whose stamina-proven profile needs others to set up the race
runners_data.comment: Won over 1m6f at Yarmouth last year; disappointing when last seen but may bounce back
runners_data.spotlight: Showed improvement when stepping up in trip last year, including a win at Yarmouth (1m6f, good); disappointing at Newmarket (1m6f, good to firm) when last seen 257 days ago but the break may have done him some good.

races.paceDynamic: The Truant stands alone as the only prominent runner in this small field, meaning he can dictate terms from the front without pressure. With four hold-up horses (John Galt, Swinging London, Vaguely Royal, Captain Brett) sitting behind him, The Truant will set a comfortable tempo that suits his own rhythm over this extended trip. The lack of pace pressure creates a tactical nightmare for the closers, who will need to time their runs perfectly from what could be a dawdling gallop. This race shape strongly favours The Truant's front-running tactics, as he can control the race without interference and kick clear when the closers are still organizing their challenges.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If The Truant gets an easy lead and maintains it
scenarios.body: The veteran controls every fraction without pressure, then has enough left to resist late challenges from the hold-up brigade. His recent Irish form suggests stamina reserves that prove decisive when he dictates terms.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuinely slow and suits closers
scenarios.body: The dawdling fractions allow the hold-up horses to produce sustained finishes, with class telling in the final furlong. Swinging London's dual course winner status becomes crucial in a tight finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Speed Wins
scenarios.trigger: If The Truant faces unexpected early pressure or fades
scenarios.body: A moderate pace develops but The Truant either gets company early or his 9-year-old legs give way, allowing the better-rated closers to capitalize. John Galt's consistency at this level proves key.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Returning Runner Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Captain Brett's 257-day break proves beneficial rather than detrimental
scenarios.body: The David Simcock-trained runner returns refreshed from his long layoff and benefits from the likely tactical pace scenario. His previous 1m6f Yarmouth win shows he has the stamina to capitalize late.

watchPoints.text: The Truant's early fractions - if genuinely dawdling he becomes almost unbeatable but quick sectionals could set up closers
Captain Brett's fitness levels after 257 days off - any early signs of rustiness or sharpness will indicate his chances immediately
How aggressively the hold-up quartet position themselves - sitting too far back in a slowly-run race could prove fatal
Swinging London's jumping from the stalls given his course form advantage - needs to be handy enough to use his local knowledge
The pace through the middle sections - genuinely slow fractions will favor stamina while moderate tempo suits the better-rated closers

races.name: Book The Bistro In Sherwood Restaurant Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Marnier
runners_data.note: Lone pace-setter returns from 17-day break with tactical advantage but questionable stamina over this extended trip
runners_data.comment: Beat two rivals in a maiden at Lingfield in November; needs to build on his Kempton return
runners_data.spotlight: Off the mark at the sixth attempt when beating two rivals in good style in a maiden at Lingfield (1m4f, AW) in November but he dropped away up the straight having taken a grip in a handicap at Kempton on his return 17 days ago; needs to build on that.

runners_data.name: Lady Ridgewood
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning from 252-day layoff under in-form Jamie Spencer but trainer form is concerning at 0/18

runners_data.name: Desert Shadow
runners_data.note: Prominent type with solid recent form but disappointed at Meydan last time and may struggle with competitive handicap company
runners_data.comment: First past the post at Beverley last year; failed to beat a rival at Meydan; back in trip
runners_data.spotlight: First past the post (demoted to second having caused interference) in a handicap at Beverley last August but he failed to beat a rival at Meydan (1m4f, good) 41 days ago; dropping back in trip should suit and he may bounce back on his return to Britain.

runners_data.name: Yaa Min
runners_data.note: Prominent racer building on recent Lingfield success with 3lb claimer but failed to follow up last time at Yarmouth
runners_data.comment: Made a winning stable debut at Lingfield last month; couldn't build on that at Yarmouth
runners_data.spotlight: Got off to the perfect start for this stable when narrowly coming out on top at Lingfield (1m4f, AW) last month but wasn't able to build on that at Yarmouth (1m2f, good) 12 days ago; place claims back on the AW.

runners_data.name: New York Minute
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with hat-trick form but faces tactical disadvantage from rear with likely slow early pace after 97-day break
runners_data.comment: Three-time winner on the AW (1m6f-2m); below his best when last seen; drops back in trip
runners_data.spotlight: Won his last two starts for Ralph Beckett and completed the hat-trick here over 2m in November when visored for the first time on his debut for this stable; ran another good race when runner-up at Kempton (2m) next time but he was below his best 97 days ago; could bounce back on his first start since but this drop back in trip may not be ideal.

runners_data.name: Elsass
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 195-day absence with solid Kempton form but faces similar tactical challenges to New York Minute
runners_data.comment: Possibly didn't handle Newmarket when last seen; gelded since; could bounce back
runners_data.spotlight: Sole win came by a nose at Chelmsford (1m2f, AW) last August and he ran well when second of nine at Kempton (1m3f, AW) next time; possibly didn't handle the undulations of Newmarket (1m4f) in the Old Rowley Cup when last seen and has since been gelded; could be capable of bouncing back returned to the AW.

races.paceDynamic: Marnier stands alone as the confirmed front-runner and will set an uncontested lead, allowing him to dictate terms throughout the 1m3f trip. Lady Ridgewood, Desert Shadow and Yaa Min are all prominent racers who will likely settle just behind the leader, creating a compact group through the early stages. With no genuine pace pressure on Marnier, he can control fractions and save energy for the finish, while the hold-up horses New York Minute and Elsass face the challenge of making ground from the back in a slowly-run affair. This tactical setup strongly favours front-runners and prominent racers who can position close to the pace without expending excessive energy.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Marnier Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Marnier gets the soft lead he's likely to receive and maintains his rhythm
scenarios.body: The uncontested leader can dictate ideal fractions and prove hard to peg back up the straight. His stamina-laden pedigree and tactical advantage make him the primary beneficiary of this race shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuine enough to stretch Marnier in the closing stages
scenarios.body: Lady Ridgewood and Desert Shadow can utilise their class advantage from prominent positions to sweep past a tiring leader. Their superior ratings and race fitness give them the edge in a tactical battle.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Charges
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is crawling and creates a sprint finish scenario
scenarios.body: New York Minute's strong recent form and finishing kick could prove decisive if he can navigate traffic from the rear. His hat-trick winning streak demonstrates current wellbeing despite the tactical disadvantage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Upset from Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the favorites fail to handle the tactical nature or distance demands
scenarios.body: Yaa Min or Elsass could benefit from the lack of early pace if connections have found significant improvement. Their lower weights become more relevant in a slowly-run contest where fitness matters.

watchPoints.text: Marnier getting too soft a lead through the early stages - if uncontested he becomes very difficult to pass
Lady Ridgewood showing any signs of ring-rust given the 252-day absence and poor recent stable form
New York Minute and Elsass getting too far back if the pace is genuine - both need tactical luck from their running styles
Desert Shadow's attitude after the Meydan disappointment - needs to bounce back to form
Yaa Min handling the step up in class after beating weaker company at Lingfield last time

races.name: Come Racing For Free 18th June Handicap

runners_data.name: Clear Above
runners_data.note: Hold-up style faces obvious traffic problems with four similar runners, plus 14 days off suggests rustiness
runners_data.comment: Failed to build on his maiden efforts when fourth of five on his handicap debut; up to 1m
runners_data.spotlight: Ran to a similar level in two maiden events at Newcastle and Southwell (both over 7f), but he failed to build on those efforts on his handicap debut at Wolverhampton (7f, AW) two weeks ago; steps up to 1m with better needed.

runners_data.name: Aneirin's Sword
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits perfectly but turf run 15 days ago on good going may have left its mark
runners_data.comment: Below his best on turf latest but was in good form on the AW prior to that; blinkers on
runners_data.spotlight: Below his best at Nottingham (8.5f, good) 15 days ago but he had been in good form on the AW prior to that, with form figures of 1222123 since the beginning of the year; may bounce back returned to the AW with blinkers on for the first time.

runners_data.name: Lexington Express
runners_data.note: Front-running style ideally placed to exploit uncontested lead, though previous hanging could be an issue
runners_data.comment: Won by 6l at Wolverhampton last month and went close there again last time; can go well
runners_data.spotlight: Posted an improved effort when winning by 6l at Wolverhampton (8.5f, AW) last month, despite hanging right, and backed that up when going close over that same C&D 19 days ago; can again go well.

runners_data.name: Action Reaction
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner making handicap debut off poor recent form, 3lb claimer suggests stable doubt
runners_data.comment: Struggled in three maiden events; much better needed on handicap debut; watch the betting
runners_data.spotlight: Struggled in three maiden events (1m/7f) in March and April (beaten 33l and 22l in two of them); much better is needed on her handicap debut but the betting should be informative.

runners_data.name: Raspoutine
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with best recent form but faces traffic nightmare with three similar tactical rivals

runners_data.name: Cobalt Comet
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner has shown nothing in three previous course runs, trainer form poor
runners_data.comment: Sent off big prices and never threatened in three novice events here; handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Sent off big prices and never threatened in three novice events at this track (two over C&D); open to improvement but he's best watched on his handicap debut.

races.paceDynamic: Lexington Express will take the field along as the sole confirmed front runner, with Aneirin's Sword likely to track in second. With no pace pressure on the leader, Lexington Express can dictate moderate fractions while the quartet of hold-up horses (Clear Above, Action Reaction, Raspoutine, Cobalt Comet) settle at the back. This creates a classic scenario where one horse controls the tempo without being harassed early. This race shape strongly favours front runners and prominent racers who can avoid traffic problems that will inevitably develop when four hold-up horses try to find racing room in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Lexington Express gets easy sectionals and maintains his kick
scenarios.body: The front runner exploits perfect positioning while hold-up horses face a wall of traffic when making their moves. Marco Ghiani can time his effort perfectly from the ideal tactical position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Charge Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes too steady and allows closers time
scenarios.body: Raspoutine and Clear Above find clear runs and exploit their superior recent form to reel in a tiring leader. The superior class of the Prescott runner particularly tells in a strongly-run finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Aneirin's Sword gets first run on the leader
scenarios.body: Saffie Osborne times her challenge perfectly as Lexington Express comes under pressure, while the hold-up quartet are caught flat-footed. The Osborne stable form and prominent position prove decisive.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If both front runners stop quickly in the final furlong
scenarios.body: A crawling pace suits none of the hold-up horses either, creating a messy finish where fitness and recent form become paramount. Raspoutine's recent Southwell win gives him the edge in a scramble.

watchPoints.text: Lexington Express breaking slowly would completely alter the pace scenario as no other natural leader exists
Traffic problems developing in the straight as four hold-up horses (Clear Above, Action Reaction, Raspoutine, Cobalt Comet) converge
Aneirin's Sword's response to pressure given the drop back from his last turf run over longer
Marco Ghiani's early positioning on Lexington Express to establish how controlled the lead will be
Whether Action Reaction or Cobalt Comet show any early speed to complicate the tactical picture

races.name: Conference & Events At Southwell Racecourse Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands B, C and D) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Ice To Meet You
runners_data.comment: Second foal; dam 7f/1m winner (including AW; RPR 91); hooded for his belated debut
runners_data.spotlight: 4yo by Postponed; second foal; dam 7f/1m winner (including AW; RPR 91), half-sister to winners Delicate Kiss (1m) and Kiss And Run (5f), out of useful 1m-1m2f winner; hooded for his belated debut.

runners_data.name: Turton
runners_data.comment: Half-brother to seven-time AW winner Whittle Le Woods; watch the betting on his debut
runners_data.spotlight: 3yo by Ribchester; sixth foal; half-brother to 6f/7f AW winner Whittle Le Woods (RPR 96); dam 7f-10.4f winner (92), half-sister to useful winners Credit Swap (6f-1m1f), Lockantanks (7f-1m) and Seafront (6f), out of 5f 2yo winner; his half-brother won seven times on the AW and he's an interesting newcomer; watch the betting.

runners_data.name: Katie's Song
runners_data.comment: Second foal; dam 1m4f winner (RPR 54); one to note in the betting on her debut
runners_data.spotlight: Second foal; dam 1m4f winner (RPR 54), half-sister to winners Continga (6f 2yo), Flanagans (Italian 5f) and Lily Trotter (2m hurdle), out of Group-placed 7f 2yo winner; one to note in the betting on her debut.

runners_data.name: Ay Up Duck
runners_data.comment: Runner-up over 7f/5f here on his two starts; steps back up in distance
runners_data.spotlight: Encouraging debut when chasing home the red-hot favourite in a C&D maiden on his debut and he ran to a similar level here over 5f two weeks ago; has hung right in both starts but should benefit from stepping back up to this trip.

runners_data.name: Marquessofanglesey
runners_data.comment: Showed some ability when sixth at Kempton over 1m on his debut; open to improvement
runners_data.spotlight: Dam 7f/1m winner (RPR 83); showed some ability when sixth of 13 at Kempton (1m, AW; 9-1) in October; drops in trip on his first start since and he's open to improvement.

runners_data.name: Got The Booty
runners_data.comment: Second at Southwell on return two weeks ago; sets the standard and should stay an easy 7f
runners_data.spotlight: Improved with each of her three starts (all 6f), recording an RPR of 73 when second of six (front two clear) at Southwell 13 days ago; open to further progress and this easy 7f should be in range; sets the standard.

runners_data.name: Rogue Desire
runners_data.comment: Showed promise on her debut last year but failed to match that on her comeback run
runners_data.spotlight: Shaped with promise on her debut at Salisbury (7f, good to firm) last August but she wasn't able to build on that on her comeback run at Wolverhampton (7f, AW) 19 days ago; may come on for that but she'll need to.

runners_data.name: Beau Chevalier
runners_data.comment: Always behind on his debut at Ascot last summer; switches to the AW having been off since
runners_data.spotlight: 150-1 and he was always behind following a slow start at Ascot (7f, good to firm) on his debut last summer; switches to the AW having been off since.

runners_data.name: Irish Incentive
runners_data.comment: Fifth at Kempton last time but she went close over this C&D last month; cheekpieces on
runners_data.spotlight: Went close in a novice over C&D last month before finishing fifth at Kempton over 1m 17 days ago, not picking up as well as might have been expected early in the straight; the drop back in trip should suit and she has cheekpieces added.

races.name: Ladies Day Sunday 16th August Handicap

runners_data.name: Enpassant
runners_data.note: Recent C&D winner under penalty who handles the going well but may find traffic problems from his hold-up style
runners_data.comment: Gained his third AW win when beating On Key over C&D last time; solid claims under penalty
runners_data.spotlight: Gained his third success on the AW when beating On Key over C&D eight days ago, despite hanging left; holds solid claims under a 5lb penalty (due to be 1lb higher in future).

runners_data.name: Bomb Squad
runners_data.note: Consistent AW performer with strong course record but trainer struggling for winners in the last 14 days
runners_data.comment: Three-time course winner; ran well when runner-up here 16 days ago; can again go well
runners_data.spotlight: Eight wins on the AW include three at this track (6f/7f), the last win coming off 2lb lower at Wolverhampton last month; ran well when runner-up here 16 days ago and there's no reason why he can't go well again.

runners_data.name: Mereside Madness
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse switching trainers after poor recent efforts, now fitted with tongue-tie for first time
runners_data.comment: Won four times for his previous stable but well held in two starts for this yard
runners_data.spotlight: Won four times for his previous stable, three of which came on the AW at Newcastle; ended his time with that yard with some lesser efforts and he's been well held in two starts for Scott Dixon; dropped another 3lb.

runners_data.name: Searchingtheblues
runners_data.note: Female hold-up runner who struggled badly last time out and may find this company too competitive
runners_data.comment: Mostly struggled since entering handicaps; drops in grade with her mark continuing to fall

runners_data.spotlight: Won two 7f handicaps at Wolverhampton in October and completed the hat-trick when winning on his return at Thirsk (7f, good) 13 days ago; can remain competitive back on the AW following a 2lb rise.

runners_data.name: On Key

runners_data.spotlight: 16-race maiden but he ran well, albeit did have every chance, when runner-up behind Enpassant over C&D eight days ago; place claims.

runners_data.name: Adelaide Bay

races.paceDynamic: Louie The Legend is the only confirmed front runner but his recent poor form and low TopSpeed rating suggest he may not set a strong gallop. On Key sits prominent but has been racing over shorter trips recently. With most runners preferring to hold up including recent winner Enpassant, hat-trick seeking Mwafaq, and consistent Bomb Squad, this sets up as a moderate pace scenario. The lack of genuine early speed will create a tactical affair that strongly favours hold-up horses who can produce a sustained finish over the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Weak Pace Favours Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Louie The Legend sets uncontested fractions and the field bunches up
scenarios.body: The moderate gallop will suit the numerous hold-up horses who can time their runs perfectly. Enpassant, Mwafaq and Bomb Squad all have the tactical speed to capitalise when the race opens up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Capitalize
scenarios.trigger: If On Key and Louie The Legend maintain position while others struggle for room
scenarios.body: The two prominently-raced horses avoid the traffic problems that could hinder the hold-up brigade in the straight. On Key's recent close second form gives him every chance to go one better.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Finish Required
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely in the middle sections creating a sprint finish
scenarios.body: Only horses with genuine turn of foot will be effective in a slowly-run contest decided in the final furlong. The classier performers with higher RPR ratings will dominate.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Early Leader Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Louie The Legend finds improvement and dictates throughout at steady fractions
scenarios.body: His front-running style could prove effective if he can find his old form and the closers leave their runs too late. The moderate pace would play into his hands perfectly.

watchPoints.text: Louie The Legend may not provide sufficient early pace which could create a muddling gallop unsuitable for his style
Enpassant carries a 5lb penalty for his recent win and may struggle to dominate from his hold-up position if pace is weak
Mwafaq partners claiming jockey Ethan Tindall for the first time despite being in excellent form
On Key showed clear improvement last time as runner-up and could benefit from prominent position if pace collapses
Bomb Squad has strong course form but trainer John Mackie is 0 from 7 in the last 14 days

runners_data.name: Raft Up
runners_data.note: Hold-up merchant who raced keenly last time over 7f, benefits from drop back to 6f but needs strong pace

runners_data.spotlight: Placed behind prolific winner Yorkshire Glory at Newcastle on two occasions (February/March) before racing keenly and running below his best here over 7f 16 days ago; should be happier back at 6f.

runners_data.name: Blackjack

runners_data.spotlight: Often front-runner; fourth of nine over C&D in January but he's struggled in three starts since; another headgear swap; others preferred.

runners_data.name: Fircombe Hall

runners_data.spotlight: Won twice at Wolverhampton (6f) last month and he was unfortunate not to finish closer when sixth over this C&D on his penultimate start; beaten a neck at Newcastle (6f, AW) three days ago and there's no reason why he can't go well again.

runners_data.name: Megaphone
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who showed improvement last time when third at Wolverhampton, needs strong gallop to be effective

runners_data.spotlight: Had beaten only one rival home in his first four starts for this stable but he took a step back in the right direction when third at Wolverhampton (6f, AW) six days ago when wearing the hood on its own (same today); chance.

races.paceDynamic: Moostar will take this race on from the gates with no other confirmed front runners in the field. Blackjack sometimes leads but hasn't shown that spark lately, leaving Moostar with an uncontested lead through steady fractions. The prominent runners Valsharah and Blackjack will track behind, while the hold-up horses Raft Up, Fircombe Hall and Megaphone will need to rely on a strong finish. This sustainable pace scenario strongly favours the front runner and prominent racers who can position close to the pace without pressure.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Moostar Wire To Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Moostar breaks cleanly and gets an easy lead with no pressure from the field
scenarios.body: She can dictate comfortable fractions and prove hard to peg back, especially with her recent form upturn since the tongue-tie addition. The lack of early pace pressure allows her to save energy for the finish and her prominent style becomes the winning move.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Kick Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes too slow in the middle stages and bunches the field for a sprint finish
scenarios.body: Fircombe Hall's hold-up style becomes the weapon as Hollie Doyle can find the clearest path through traffic in the final furlong. His recent Wolverhampton wins show he has the acceleration to strike when the pace collapses.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Valsharah can position perfectly behind Moostar and time his challenge in the final 100 yards
scenarios.body: The tongue-tie has transformed his recent efforts and Jason Watson can use his 21-race experience to finally break his maiden tag. His second at Kempton proves he has the finishing kick when positioned right.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Early
scenarios.trigger: If Moostar goes too fast early or Blackjack surprisingly challenges for the lead creating pace pressure
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure stamina test where Raft Up's hold-up style under Ethan Tindall becomes effective despite his 5-pound claim. His Newcastle placings behind Yorkshire Glory show he responds to a truly run race.

watchPoints.text: Moostar breaking slowly would completely change the pace dynamic as no other natural leader emerges from this field
Blackjack showing early speed could create unexpected pace pressure and compromise Moostar's tactics
Fircombe Hall's position turning for home will indicate if the pace has been strong enough for his finishing kick
Valsharah's positioning behind the leader will show if Watson can finally convert his recent improvement into a maiden win
Raft Up racing keenly again would repeat his disappointing effort from 16 days ago over the longer trip
